correctness.rationale: For prime p>35 the cyclotomic quotient identity and explicit inverse period h derive the exact block words. Inserting one full 35-period into each of 24 nonempty words proves the affine law for all q. Exact standard-library arithmetic exhausts all 24 unit residues, verifies 576 B/A entries, nonemptiness, second-gap exclusions and multiplicities; independent quotient long division checks 72 representative 35q+r indices. The finite certificate is used only for finitely many residue classes, not induction over q.

originality.rationale: The cited 2019 main theorem determines only the maximum gap, whereas the new theorem computes every frequency and the next-largest gap for a fixed ternary family. The 3pq results exclude 35p because their smallest prime is 3; the 2025 second-gap theorem applies to binary rather than ternary cyclotomic polynomials. Camburu et al. (2015) quantify largest gaps and binary semigroup gap structure, with no full ternary 35p gap spectrum. OEIS A011634 records coefficients of the base polynomial, not a 35p spectrum. No equivalent statement was found in the actual searches. Historical priority beyond accessible material remains uncertain.
residual_risks: A different terminology (support intervals or coefficient blocks) could encode an equivalent all-frequency result in unindexed literature.
The 2019 block decomposition is already known; originality rests on the concrete complete 35p gap-frequency classification, not on the decomposition itself.
The inspection of the later binary article focused on its main statements rather than every appendix.

value.rationale: Cyclotomic sparsity beyond the largest gap is a recognized structural question (2019 maximum-gap and 2025 binary second-gap studies). For the first ternary family with fixed base 35, a complete gap-length histogram and the precise second distinct gap give a substantially finer invariant than the known maximum, with direct comparison across all primes and residue classes. The exact affine law makes arbitrary large-prime computations finite and distinguishes residue-dependent collision patterns. It is not a mere increment to an arbitrary parameter: it characterizes the full natural support-spacing distribution.
